findings.claim: The Str8 case (`case <= byte.MaxValue`) was removed from the string header writer. Strings of 32..255 bytes now fall through to the Str16 branch, so the encoding is non-minimal and larger than before. This is a wire-format change that has nothing to do with the analyzer requirement. It is also a regression for any consumer or interop that expects the compact Str8 form. It inflates payloads and can break byte-exact round-trip and format tests. The effect is a size and format regression, not a memory-safety hole, so I rate it high as a breaking change.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a 100-byte ASCII string with base-built and head-built MessagePackPrimitives.TryWriteStringHeader / MessagePackWriter.WriteString. Base emits 0xD9 0x64 (Str8); head emits 0xDA 0x00 0x64 (Str16). Compare the bytes.

findings.claim: Duplicate-key members are now silently dropped via the `ContainsKey` guard instead of the `Add` throwing, so the generator no longer fails loudly on duplicates. Whether the duplicate-key diagnostic (MsgPack006) is still reported depends on code outside this diff. If it is not reported, a type with duplicate keys can generate a formatter that silently omits a member. That is a correctness problem rather than a security hole, but it is worth checking, since the old throw may have been caught and surfaced.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator/analyzer test on a [MessagePackObject] type with two members sharing [Key(0)]. Assert that MsgPack006 is still reported and that the generator does not throw or silently omit a member.
